title: The Smithy — Low Kiln, Sill
caption: The forge east of the Clay Yard, drawn at the scale of a man standing at the bench: the long low shop with no kiln-mark over its door, the forge hearth and bellows, the anvil, the bench with its chisel notches that nobody has ever entered as a figure, the kiln behind the bench answering four pulls with the fifth missing, three collectors' cold-iron tubes on their pegs with the grips polished grey to the thumb, Keldish bars with the blue bloom no potter will glaze over, the ash pit, the trough and the slate lying face down on a shop where no man would write a sentence. The yard well, the Vail kiln-house, the wheel-shed, the drying racks, House Silt, House Reed and the birth-flower shrine stand faint at the edges; the Clay Road runs west to the Cross and east to Greybank, with the Slip Brook and the Ilm below. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Frost, with compass, a scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the tubes that take and do not give, the pale ring left at a wrist, the count kept in wood, the iron that comes down from Keld and the counting room shut in the last war eighteen leagues east. An engraved tube and an engraved anvil sit in the margin.
